Nearly two dozen brands and close to 100 million consumers make the jump, among them TheStreet, Parade, Men’s Journal, Athlon Sports, Autoblog and Powder, plus hundreds of reporters currently on staff.

Roundtable projects the arrangement will pull in $100 million a year in revenue and push the company to an EBITDA-positive run rate on its own, once the ink dries and 100 million monthly users start flowing through the system.

Heckman called the deal the culmination of decades spent building toward this kind of scale, arguing it gives premium publishers and advertisers an environment they can trust. Sornsin said publishers have spent years losing ground on economics, data and audience control to big tech and now to AI, and he added that this partnership hands that control back.

A separate minority stake ties the whole arrangement together. Roundtable will pay $89 million in cash and stock to take roughly 49% ownership of Paradium in a private transaction. That piece, along with remaining closing conditions and funding requirements, is set to wrap up in the fourth quarter.
Paradium.AI shares were up 271.15% at $0.91 at the time of publication on Thursday, according to Benzinga Pro.
